Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of sudden neck and chest pain following forceful Valsalva maneuvers (dry heaving, sneezing) combined with radiographic findings of linear lucencies along the hilar/paratracheal regions and subcutaneous emphysema is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect). Esophageal perforation typically presents with more severe systemic toxicity and pleural effusions, while traumatic pneumothorax would show a visible pleural line and lung collapse not seen here.
